drafts.headline: Cash cost forecasts run about 55% too low for ARCC.
drafts.plain: The method misses this driver in the same direction almost every time, not at random. That is a fixable defect rather than noise — find what is wired wrong before adding any correction factor.
drafts.evidence: Bias -0.439 log (about 55% too low), average miss 0.551, wrong in the same direction in 68% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=25).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: A later run of the same name where the sign no longer holds across bootstrap blocks.
drafts.declined: Same finding as DRAFT-ARCC-02 one level up: total cash cost is cost per tonne times volume, so its bias is the cpt bias plus the volume bias and is not independent evidence. Registered once, at the driver where the cause lives.

drafts.headline: In a devaluing currency a cement cost-per-tonne escalator built on the last known exchange-rate move runs far too low.
drafts.plain: Most of a cement producer's cash cost is imported fuel, priced in dollars. Escalating it by the exchange-rate move you last saw is the only honest thing to do at the time, and it will still be badly wrong when the currency goes on to fall by a factor of three. That is a limit of what can be forecast, not a defect to be corrected — 71% of this error disappears if you hand the model the exchange rate it could not have known.
drafts.evidence: Bias -0.315 log (about 37% too low), average miss 0.406, wrong in the same direction in 72% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=25).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: A cement producer whose fuel is genuinely priced in local currency, where the same escalator still runs this far low.

drafts.headline: A debt path that amortises to zero and never re-borrows will forecast no interest for ever.
drafts.plain: If the rule for future debt is 'keep repaying at the recent average', it eventually reaches zero and stays there — so the model shows a company with no borrowings and no interest cost, however much it later borrows. The fix is a debt schedule read from the disclosed facilities and their maturities, not a multiplier on the interest line.
drafts.evidence: Bias -0.545 log (about 1.7 times too low), average miss 0.813, wrong in the same direction in 64% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=14).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: A build whose debt path is read from disclosed facilities and maturities, where the finance-cost bias is still this large.

drafts.headline: The fin forecast loses to assuming no change.
drafts.plain: At 3 of 5 horizons, simply carrying last year's number forward beat the model. A method that cannot beat 'no change' has not earned the precision it displays, and should be published as a range or not at all.
drafts.evidence: Negative skill against the freeze benchmark at horizons 1, 2, 3, worst -2.290.
drafts.why_scope: Losing to a naive benchmark usually points at the method, which would make it ALL — but confirm it is not this company's series being unusually persistent.
drafts.overturned_by: A later run where the model beats the freeze benchmark at a majority of horizons.
drafts.declined: The finance-cost forecast loses to freeze for the reason registered in DRAFT-ARCC-03 — the debt path reaches zero and stays there. One defect, one lesson.

drafts.headline: The other forecast loses to assuming no change.
drafts.plain: At 4 of 5 horizons, simply carrying last year's number forward beat the model. A method that cannot beat 'no change' has not earned the precision it displays, and should be published as a range or not at all.
drafts.evidence: Negative skill against the freeze benchmark at horizons 2, 3, 4, 5, worst -0.872.
drafts.why_scope: Losing to a naive benchmark usually points at the method, which would make it ALL — but confirm it is not this company's series being unusually persistent.
drafts.overturned_by: A later run where the model beats the freeze benchmark at a majority of horizons.
drafts.declined: Non-cement revenue is a small residual line (0.9-3.5% of sales) escalated at inflation. Losing to freeze on a line this small is not a finding about the method; it is a line that deserves no driver at all, and the study says so.

drafts.headline: For ARCC, last year's own volume beats a national-market-times-share build.
drafts.plain: Anchoring volume on Egypt's cement market and ACC's share of it is supposed to be more disciplined than extrapolating the company. On this name it is worse, because ACC's own share moved much further than the market did — from 8.1% to 5.4% as it pivoted from domestic cement to clinker exports. The anchor was steady and the company was not.
drafts.evidence: Negative skill against the freeze benchmark at horizons 3, 4, 5, worst -1.673.
drafts.why_scope: Losing to a naive benchmark usually points at the method, which would make it ALL — but confirm it is not this company's series being unusually persistent.
drafts.overturned_by: A later ARCC run in which the market-share anchor beats the freeze benchmark, or a second cement name showing the same thing — which would make it a class finding rather than this company's.

drafts.headline: The fin error is the company, not the currency.
drafts.plain: Re-running every forecast with perfect foresight of inflation barely improves it. So devaluation is not the explanation, and looking for a macro fix would waste the effort.
drafts.evidence: Average miss 0.813 as known, 0.813 with perfect foresight of inflation — the macro share is only 0.0%.
drafts.why_scope: Almost always ALL — 'check whether the macro explains it before assuming it does' is a method rule — but the specific finding may be about this market.
drafts.overturned_by: A market or period where the same decomposition puts most of the error on the macro path.
drafts.declined: Restates DRAFT-ARCC-03 through the macro split: the finance-cost error has a zero macro share because the driver reaches zero, not because the currency is irrelevant to it. Filing it as 'the company, not the currency' would record the wrong cause.

drafts.headline: The gp error is the company, not the currency.
drafts.plain: Re-running every forecast with perfect foresight of inflation barely improves it. So devaluation is not the explanation, and looking for a macro fix would waste the effort.
drafts.evidence: Average miss 1.094 as known, 1.293 with perfect foresight of inflation — the macro share is only -18.2%.
drafts.why_scope: Almost always ALL — 'check whether the macro explains it before assuming it does' is a method rule — but the specific finding may be about this market.
drafts.overturned_by: A market or period where the same decomposition puts most of the error on the macro path.
drafts.declined: Same measurement as DRAFT-ARCC-13 one line up the income statement. Gross profit and net profit share the offsetting-error mechanism; registered once, at net profit, where it matters to a reader.

drafts.headline: When revenue and cost carry different currency weights, fixing the macro can make the profit forecast worse.
drafts.plain: If a model under-forecasts both revenue and cost, the two misses partly cancel and the profit looks better than the model deserves. Correct the currency path on both sides and the cancellation breaks, because the cost side usually carries far more of the exchange rate than the revenue side does. So a profit forecast that looks accurate may be accurate by offsetting errors — check the two sides separately before believing it.
drafts.evidence: Average miss 1.106 as known, 1.504 with perfect foresight of inflation — the macro share is only -36.0%.
drafts.why_scope: Almost always ALL — 'check whether the macro explains it before assuming it does' is a method rule — but the specific finding may be about this market.
drafts.overturned_by: A build where revenue and cost carry the same currency weight and the profit error still gets worse under perfect macro foresight.

drafts.headline: The cash cost bias changes direction between regimes.
drafts.plain: It runs one way in one period and the other way in the next. Averaging them produces a correction that is wrong in both. Record it, do not correct for it.
drafts.evidence: By era: E2 post-float +0.114; E3 devaluation -0.614.
drafts.why_scope: A sign that flips with the regime is usually about the market or the period, not the company — but say which.
drafts.overturned_by: A longer record in which one sign dominates across all regimes.
drafts.declined: L-029 already says a bias that changes sign between regimes is not a bias and must not be corrected for. This run confirms it on a second company; that confirmation belongs in the evidence for L-029 at its next revision, not as a new lesson.

drafts.headline: A correction to cpt worked and must still be checked against the rest of the book.
drafts.plain: A fudge factor that improves this one name can be hiding a defect in how we set the model up. Before adopting it, check it matches how that driver is built everywhere else.
drafts.evidence: Applied +0.011 at origin 2022; average miss changed -0.011.
drafts.why_scope: If the correction turns out to be fixing our own mis-specification, the lesson is ALL and is about specification. If the company is genuinely unusual, it is STOCK.
drafts.overturned_by: Evidence that the driver is built the same way across the book and this name still needs the correction.
drafts.declined: L-003 already requires every correction to be checked against how the driver class is built across the book, and this run is the second time that clause did its job — it refused this exact correction. A lesson restating a rule that worked is noise.
